A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ENEL research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are available for comparison, and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original ENEL experiments on Objaverse classification and captioning, 3D MM-Vet VQA, architectural ablations, and resolution sensitivity.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical evaluations and reports revised ablation results, additional configurations, and ENEL-13B results in Table 5.

M1.justification: The default Hierarchical Geometry Aggregation configuration changes from one aggregation/propagation pair to three. V1 compresses 128 tokens to 64; v2 compresses them through 64, 32, and 16 before restoring them across layers 6–8. This reconfigures an existing component while retaining the token embedding, Hybrid Semantic Loss, gated aggregation operations, and two-stage framework.

E1.justification: Both retain the PointLLM training data, Objaverse classification/captioning, 3D MM-Vet VQA, and the 2K–16K resolution test. Added model scales and qualitative examples do not establish distinct dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 5 retains the same InstructBLIP, LLaVA, 3D-LLM, PointLLM, and ShapeLLM comparators, including their model sizes and task participation. Figure 1 still compares PointLLM with ENEL. ENEL-13B is an added configuration of the proposed model.

E3.justification: V2 adds 13B evaluation, extends the learnable-layer sweep to 12 layers, and tests four aggregation steps. The default aggregation depth changes from one to three. Reported epoch budgets, batch sizes, learning rates, preprocessing, metrics, and GPT-4 judge versions remain unchanged; classification prompt averaging is newly explained rather than established as a protocol change.

E4.justification: V2 extends the depth ablations in Tables 2 and 4, adds response cases in Figure 6, and introduces a caption/reference case study in Appendix B.2. Conversely, Table 3 removes the isolated positional-encoding ablation: the with-position result remains, but its without-position control disappears.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run counts, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. V2's newly explained classification average concerns two prompts, not uncertainty across runs.

E6.justification: Table 4 reverses the preferred aggregation depth from one to three, while Tables 4 and 6 and Figure 1 revise numerous results. Table 5 updates ENEL-7B captioning/classification/VQA scores from 50.92/55.00/42.70 to 50.98/55.10/43.10 and adds ENEL-13B scores of 52.87/55.30/48.20. These materially extend and revise the empirical findings. Because the default hierarchy changes, the 7B updates do not establish isolated same-configuration gains.

T1.justification: The mathematical loss definitions and aggregation equations (1–8), including the appendix variants, are retained. Neither version introduces new theoretical assumptions, theorems, or proofs. Revised layer counts concern architectural configuration.

C1.justification: Both claim the first encoder-free 3D LMM investigation, transfer of encoding functions into the LLM through the same two strategies, and competitive performance against encoder-based models. Updated headline scores and replacement-oriented wording do not materially redefine these central contributions.

C2.justification: The interpretation of aggregation depth changes substantially: v1 attributes deterioration with more operations to lost detail and interpolation noise; v2 motivates three operations by insufficient spatial modeling with fewer steps. New Appendix B.2 also explains metric disagreements through caption length and semantic matching, favoring GPT-4 evaluation and invoking human judgments without documenting a supporting human-study protocol.

D1.justification: V2's Appendix A specifies the revised aggregation/propagation layers and token counts. Table 1 newly explains classification averaging over two prompts, and Appendix B.2 describes GPT-4 scoring. Existing hardware, optimizer, token-embedding details, training budgets, and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: The introduction adds multimodal-generation context citing Janus-Pro, Can We Generate Images with CoT?, and T2I-R1, while removing background citations such as Sam2Point, Lift3D, and MathVerse. Core positioning relative to PointLLM, ShapeLLM, and encoder-free vision-language models remains stable. Related Work is relocated rather than newly introduced.

P1.justification: Related Work moves from Appendix A to Section 2, with corresponding section renumbering. V2 adds Metric Analysis and Response Visualization passages, tightens existing prose, and renames Further 3D Encoding to emphasize alignment. Most of the original narrative and explanations remain recognizable.

P2.justification: V2 redesigns the resolution/attention display and pipeline figures, restyles other method diagrams, and adds response Figure 6. Figure 4 and Table 4 are resized and rearranged, and table headers and emphasis change. Original appendix Figures 6 and 7 remain as Figures 7 and 8. Together these constitute a broad visual revision.

improvement.justification: Extending evaluation from 7B to 13B provides additional evidence about scaling, while expanded depth ablations and clearer prompt and implementation descriptions improve assessability. These gains are limited by removal of the positional-encoding control and unsupported human-evaluation statements in Appendix B.2. The small score updates alone do not establish better performance, particularly with the changed hierarchy.
